subject: VIP: NeonCredit throughput & latency — reserved pool shortfall
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria@neoncredit.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: NeonCredit Ops <ops@neoncredit.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VIP: sustained latency and 5xx on reserved pool

Hi Rishi —

We're seeing a sustained spike in tail latency and a growing 5xx rate on our reserved GPU pool since ~07:30 PT. Impact: several customer-facing inference flows are timing out and a subset of requests are returning 5xx. This is affecting our payments risk scoring (high priority) and one live cohort is timing out on checkout.

I've attached a short error log and a screenshot of our request rate/latency. Key numbers now: p95 latency ~2.8s (normally 350ms), 5xx rate ~4.6% (baseline <0.1%). Token throughput for our reserved queue is plateauing despite unchanged request volume.

We have an urgent Q: can Redwood immediately prioritize our reserved pool or provide a documented mitigation (burst credit, fallback model, or temporary capacity shift)? We need to let ops and our CTO know by EOD.

Thanks —
Maria Santos
Head of Engineering Operations
NeonCredit

Attachments: neoncredit_error_log_0716.txt, neoncredit_kpi_screenshot_0716.png

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Santos <maria@neoncredit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VIP: sustained latency and 5xx on reserved pool

Maria — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I'm pulling in Eng and Sales to triage immediately. Short answers up front: we can (1) prioritize NeonCredit's reserved queue on the GPU farm, (2) enable a temporary burst reserve while we investigate, and (3) fail over lower-priority traffic to an alternate model variant if needed.

Requests: can you confirm the HubSpot deal id (I have DEAL-8934) and whether the affected routes are pin-to-model or using autoscaling? Also please attach any recent request IDs you want us to drill into.

We will:
- Irene/David: run a root cause on kernel/kv-cache pressure and kernel selection mismatch (15m)
- Marissa: prepare an exec-facing impact note and credit proposal (30m)
- My ask to NeonCredit: hold on any configuration changes on your side unless we request them — we may switch routing to a compatible hosted variant.

I'll follow up with a short plan in 40m.

—Rishi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Santos <maria@neoncredit.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VIP: sustained latency and 5xx on reserved pool

Adding context from the account side: NeonCredit is on a Reserved Dedicated plan with a monthly commit and is considered a strategic mid-market customer (high touch). If this impacts checkout for multiple customers there is immediate revenue risk and PR exposure. Customer asks we've heard on the call:
- Immediate throughput relief (burst or prioritized headroom)
- Clear SLA remediation path and an estimate for when p95/p99 will return to normal
- A goodwill credit if the impact spans >4 hours

Irene / David — plz include a crisp cause hypothesis in your notes so I can communicate to the NeonCredit CTO and CFO without jargon. I will draft an initial credit proposal: 25% invoice credit pro-rated for the impacted window, pending ops signoff.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Maria Santos <maria@neoncredit.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VIP: sustained latency and 5xx on reserved pool

On Thu, Jul 16, 2026 at 9:12 AM Maria Santos <maria@neoncredit.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a sustained spike in tail latency and a growing 5xx rate on our reserved GPU pool since ~07:30 PT.

Short technical summary (initial):
- Symptoms: KV-cache pressure and frequent kernel preemption on the specific GPU slice serving NeonCredit's reserved queue. That aligns with the observed p95/p99 increase and step-up in error rate.
- Telemetry: queue depth for NeonCredit's reservation increased by ~4.5x in the window between 07:15–08:05 PT; CPU-bound dispatch delays observed on the orchestration host.
- Likely root causes we are pursuing: noisy neighbor within the same NUMA zone causing GPU context thrash OR a regression in the kernel selection heuristics after a model variant rollout last night.

Immediate mitigations deployed (10:35 PT):
1) Elevated NeonCredit queue priority on the scheduler (soft priority) — should reduce queuing within 5–10m.
2) Enabled a short burst reservation of 2x their standard headroom for 60 minutes (temporary).
3) If errors persist we will route non-critical endpoints to the hosted model variant (lower-latency profile) — requires NeonCredit consent for any data routing change.

Next steps (ETA):
- Short RCAs: kernel heuristics + NUMA isolation (30–60m)
- If we confirm noisy neighbor: migrate neighbor workload to an alternate host (45–90m)
- Post-mortem & codefix if heuristics regression found (TBD)

I will attach a telemetry extract once David confirms (attaching soon).

Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Maria Santos <maria@neoncredit.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VIP: sustained latency and 5xx on reserved pool

Attaching the telemetry CSV and a short extract here. Highlights:
- 07:10–07:45 PT window: NeonCredit reserved queue Q depth avg 42 -> peak 187
- Kernel preemption events per GPU increased 8x vs baseline
- Replica placement shows one host with three high-memory model replicas colocated in the same NUMA zone (candidate noisy neighbor)

Attachment: neoncredit_telemetry_0716.csv

Sample entries (timestamps truncated):
2026-07-16T07:18:12Z,queue_depth,neon-reserved,120
2026-07-16T07:22:21Z,kernel_preemptions,gpu-37,18
2026-07-16T07:27:05Z,error_rate,neon-reserved,0.032

I recommend we: (A) keep the burst reserve active for the next 60–90m, (B) live-migrate one noisy neighbor replica off the host (low risk), and (C) run a targeted kernel-heuristic rollback on a canary host if we see consistent regression markers.

—David
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Santos <maria@neoncredit.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VIP: sustained latency and 5xx on reserved pool — executive briefing scheduled

Maria — quick update and path forward. Apologies for the delay getting back; we staffed this through the weekend to verify stability.

What we did so far (summary):
- Elevated queue priority and applied a 2x burst reservation (rolled back at 09:35 PT after traffic normalized).
- Live-migrated a noisy neighbor replica off the affected host (reduced kernel preemptions by ~70%).
- Telemetry shows p95 dropped from 2.8s -> 420ms and 5xx rate fell below 0.2% within 35m of mitigation.

Customer-facing remediation & offer:
- We're scheduling an exec brief (30m) with NeonCredit CTO + Redwood VP Sales on Mon 07/20 11:00 PT to review root cause and long-term mitigations. Link: https://meet.redwood/meetings/neoncredit-ctobrief
- As a goodwill gesture we will provide a pro-rated 30% credit for the impacted 6-hour window, plus one free month of prioritized burst for the next billing cycle. Marissa will follow with the credit note and T&Cs.
- Engineering action items: full post-mortem (RCA) due 72 hours, kernel heuristic regression checklist, and better NUMA isolation logic in the priority scheduler.

Maria — please confirm that Monday at 11:00 PT works and whether you want additional stakeholders at the brief (CFO/Head of Customer Success). If you prefer a different time, let us know and we'll accommodate.

Thanks for working with us through this. We know this is critical and will keep this at highest priority until NeonCredit is fully stable.

—Rishi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
